title: Cannabis Etiquette: Sharing, Hosting and Being a Good Neighbor | CastleLeaf
h1: Cannabis Etiquette: Sharing, Hosting and Being a Good Neighbor
description: Cannabis manners for Allston-Brighton: how to share, how to host, why consent matters, never driving and why public consumption is illegal in Massachusetts.
excerpt: Cannabis is better in good company, and good company has a few unwritten rules. Here they are, written down, from passing a joint to keeping the peace with the neighbors.
pull: The best host isn’t the one with the most impressive stash; it’s the one whose guests all get home safely.

blocks.html: Cannabis is for everyone, but not everyone wants it right now. Good etiquette starts with a simple question, “Would you like some?”, and then takes the answer at face value, whether it’s yes, no or maybe later.

Consent matters even more with edibles. Never give anyone infused food or drink without telling them, and never pressure a friend to have more than they want. Everyone responds differently, and “I’m good, thanks” deserves the same respect as “yes, please.”
There’s a reason “puff, puff, pass” has lasted so long: it keeps things moving and fair. A few more habits make you a welcome guest:

items: Pass to the left, unless the room has its own tradition. When in doubt, follow the host.
Don’t hold on to it mid-story. If you’re telling a long one, pass first and talk second.
Bring something to share if you can, like a few pre-rolls. Nobody has to roll, and anyone who prefers their own can have one.
If you have a cold, sit the round out or keep to your own.

blocks.html: The best host isn’t the one with the most impressive stash; it’s the one whose guests all get home safely. If you’re inviting friends over, a little planning goes a long way.

items: Label everything. Keep infused snacks clearly marked and apart from regular food. If they’re store-bought, share the serving size from the label.
Offer alternatives. Water, alcohol-free drinks and ordinary snacks keep everyone comfortable, whatever they choose.
Have the basics ready. A proper ashtray, a lighter that works and a seat by an open window. Our accessories cover the small things that make a big difference.
Keep it 21+. Cannabis is for adults 21 and over, and that goes for every guest.
Tidy up afterward. Put leftovers somewhere secure, out of reach of children and pets.

sections.heading: Never drive, and plan the ride home

blocks.html: This one is less etiquette than law. As our FAQ puts it: “Consuming while driving is illegal and dangerous.” Plan the ride home before the evening starts: a designated driver who isn’t consuming, a rideshare, a walk or the T.
If you’re carrying cannabis in your car, keep it in a sealed container, and never consume in a vehicle.

Massachusetts is clear on this, and so are we: “Public consumption is illegal in MA. We ask that you respect the law and the community that we operate in. Please consume responsibly on private property only.”

That means no sidewalks, parks, beaches, bus stops or parking lots. The best spot is a private space where you’re welcome to consume, like your own home or a host’s. If you rent, check your lease and building rules first.

sections.heading: Being a good neighbor in Allston-Brighton

blocks.html: Allston-Brighton is a lively, close-quarters place: apartments, triple-deckers, shared porches and plenty of open windows in summer. A little courtesy keeps the peace.

items: Mind the smell. Smoke drifts through shared walls, hallways and open windows. Some people find that edibles or a vaporizer leave less lingering aroma than smoking.
Keep the volume down. Late-night porch sessions carry further than you think.
Clean up. Dispose of ash and ends properly, never on the sidewalk or in a neighbor’s planter.

blocks.html: Brighton Belongs to You, and to your neighbors too. Look after the neighborhood the way you’d want your own front step looked after, and everyone gets to enjoy it.

faq.q: Can I consume cannabis in public in Massachusetts?
faq.a_html: No. Public consumption is illegal in MA. Please consume responsibly on private property only, and only where you have permission.

faq.q: Is it okay to share cannabis with friends?
faq.a_html: With adults 21 and over who want it, in a private space, sharing is part of the culture. Always ask first, never pressure anyone, and never give infused food to someone without telling them.
No. Consuming while driving is illegal and dangerous, and you should never drive impaired. Plan a sober driver, a rideshare or public transit before you start.
